data.summary: The six‑week plan balances new content with practice, covering every unit at least once while keeping weekly load at 20 hours. Early weeks introduce foundational topics and include the scheduled live classes. Mid‑plan weeks deepen understanding and add free‑response drills. The final two weeks focus on mixed review and timed practice to build stamina for the October 13 exam.

weeks.focus: Foundations: atomic structure, periodic trends, and intermolecular forces
tasks: Read textbook sections on atomic structure and periodic trends; take concise notes.
Do 15 practice problems on electron configuration and periodic trends; check answers.
Complete the live class #9500 and review the class notes.
Watch a 20‑minute video on intermolecular forces; summarize key differences.
Do 10 free‑response questions on intermolecular forces; grade with the scoring guide.
Read chapters on chemical bonds, Lewis diagrams, and VSEPR; create a chart of bond types.
Complete 12 Lewis‑structure problems, including resonance structures.
Do 8 VSEPR shape exercises; verify with answer key.
Work through 10 ideal‑gas‑law problems, including KMT derivations.
Take a 30‑minute timed quiz covering bonds and gases; review mistakes.
Read sections on reaction types and net ionic equations; make a summary table.
Complete the live class #9501 and add class notes to study binder.
Do 12 stoichiometry problems involving limiting reagents and percent yield.
Watch a short video on reaction rates; write 5 notes on rate‑law terminology.
Solve 8 rate‑law introductory problems; check with solution guide.
Read textbook chapters on enthalpy, energy diagrams, and calorimetry; create flashcards for key equations.
Complete 10 calorimetry calculations using heat capacity data.
Do 8 problems on concentration‑time graphs and elementary reactions.
Watch a tutorial on activation energy; summarize the concept in 3 sentences.
Take a 25‑minute timed set of mixed thermochemistry and kinetics free‑response questions; grade yourself.
Read sections on chemical equilibrium and equilibrium constants; fill out equilibrium‑constant worksheet.
Solve 10 problems calculating Kc and using reaction quotients.
Complete acid‑base equilibrium practice set (weak acids/bases and buffer calculations).
Work through 6 Gibbs free‑energy problems linking ΔG to K.
Do 4 electrochemistry cell‑potential calculations; verify with answer key.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed AP practice
tasks: Do a full‑length (90‑minute) AP Chemistry practice exam under timed conditions.
Mark the exam using the official scoring guide; note topics of incorrect answers.
Review each missed question by revisiting the corresponding textbook section or notes.
Complete a mixed‑topic drill set of 20 free‑response questions covering all units.
Create a one‑page “cheat sheet” of key equations and concepts for final review.

data.final_week_advice: After the timed practice, focus on the few remaining weak spots, review your cheat sheet daily, and get plenty of rest the night before the exam. Arrive early, bring all required materials, and manage your time wisely during the test.
